Note test: `I.parse(["--k=--v"])` -> values k=["--v"]. So `--key=value` accepts anything after `=`.

Also note `["--x","y","--x"]` -> values x=["y"], flags x=True. So when a value is consumed, the key also becomes... wait, flags x=True? Interesting. {"values": {"x": ["y"]}, "flags": {"x": True}} — so a flag with a value also gets a switch True? Hmm. Let's re-read: "--x","y" -> values x=["y"]; then "--x" with no value -> switch True. So flags x=True from the second occurrence. That doesn't tell whether the first sets a flag. Let's check test_equals_and_space_forms_agree: `["--mode=fast","-v"]` -> flags {"v": True} only, no mode. So value keys don't get flags. Good.

So implementation: iterate; for each token:
- if after `--` terminator: positional.
- if token == "--": set terminator, drop.
- if token startswith "--":
  - strip "--"; if "=" in body: key, val = split on first "="; values[key].append(val)
  - else key = body; look ahead next token: if exists and not startswith("--"): consume it as value (append), advance. else flags[key]=True.
  - Edge: what about next token starting with "-" single dash like "-5" -> accepted as value. Only "--"-prefixed rejected.
- elif token startswith "-" and token != "-": bundled switches: for ch in token[1:]: flags[ch]=True. (What about "-5"? Hmm, "-5" as a standalone token... not in tests. Treat as bundled switch "5". Fine.)
- else positional.

Also `--k=--v` value accepted regardless.

Also empty key like "--" already handled. "--=x"? Not tested.

Order of positional preserved.
